questions.question: When it is obvious that you are going to turn, you:

options.text: Do not need to use a turn signal.
Should still use a turn signal.
Only need to use a turn signal if there are nearby pedestrians.
Only need to use a turn signal if you are at a stop light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should still use a turn signal.
questions.explanation: Always use a turn signal when you turn or change lanes. Use it even if you think your intentions are obvious. Other vehicles may be nearby that you cannot see.

questions.question: Most crashes happen during the day. To reduce your chance of a crash, you should:
questions.explanation: Make yourself as visible as possible by wearing bright-colored clothing when riding, even during the day.

questions.question: Studies show that when motorcycles have their headlights on during the day:

options.text: They are not as easy to see as other vehicles.
They are more visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
They are less safe than with headlights off.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more visible to other drivers than with headlights off.
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on whenever you ride. A motorcycle with its headlight on is twice as likely to be noticed by other drivers during the day.

questions.question: To help other drivers see you, you should wear:
questions.explanation: Wear bright-colored clothing to be seen by other drivers. Bright colors increase your visibility during the day and at night.

questions.question: Which surface provides the best traction for a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Dry pavement provides the best traction. Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, lane markings, and metal covers can be hazardous for motorcycles.

questions.question: A way to reduce your risk of a crash is to:

options.text: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Ride in areas where other drivers cannot see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Communicate your plans by using turn signals, brake lights, and proper lane position. Stay visible to others. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: Drivers entering the highway may not see you. What should you do to help them merge safely?

options.text: Stay in your lane. It is not your responsibility to be seen.
Change to another lane away from the entrance ramp, if you can.
Weave within your lane to get their attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change to another lane away from the entrance ramp, if you can.
questions.explanation: Give merging vehicles plenty of space. Change lanes away from the entrance ramp if it is safe to do so. If you cannot change lanes, slow down to create space for the merging driver.

questions.question: When passing parked cars, a motorcycle operator should be ready for:

options.text: A parked car to suddenly pull into traffic.
Other drivers to see you and move out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: A parked car to suddenly pull into traffic.
questions.explanation: Be ready for a parked car to suddenly move into traffic. Ride in the left part of your lane when passing parked cars on your right. This creates more space between you and any car that might pull out.

questions.question: As you slow or stop, you should:

options.text: Take the bike out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears with the clutch as you slow or stop. Stay in first gear while stopped so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: A motorcycle fits you properly if:

options.text: You can touch your feet to the ground while seated.
You can reach the controls by stretching.
The handlebars go over your head.
Your feet cannot rest on the foot pegs.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can touch your feet to the ground while seated.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle fits you properly when your feet can reach the ground while seated. You should be able to easily reach and operate all controls.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks does the body eliminate per hour, on average?
questions.explanation: The body can eliminate about one drink per hour. The time needed to lower your blood alcohol content (BAC) varies. It is safest to not drive after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: Before every ride, you should check all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your motorcycle carefully. Check the rims and spokes for bends, looseness, or damage. Check the tire condition and tread. Check all the lights.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, you should:

options.text: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
Increase your speed to leave the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake of the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and keep the motorcycle straight as you slow down. If you need to brake, slowly apply the brake of the tire that is not flat, if you know which one it is.

questions.question: Intersections are usually:

options.text: Safe because there is so much traffic there.

questions.explanation: Intersections are dangerous because they have the most potential for conflicts between motorcyclists and other drivers.

questions.question: You should use a turn signal:

options.text: When you plan to increase your speed.
Only when there is heavy traffic.
Any time you plan to change lanes.
Only when it is dark outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Any time you plan to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Use a turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one else is around to see it.

questions.question: Taking corners too fast:

options.text: Can cause you to go into another lane.
Is better than going too slowly.
Usually keeps you in your lane.
Is acceptable because motorcycles are smaller.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can cause you to go into another lane.
questions.explanation: Taking a corner too fast may cause you to cross into another lane or go off the road. Slow down before you start to turn.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger on a motorcycle, you must:

options.text: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
Have only one set of footrests.
Not tell the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Only carry a passenger if your motorcycle has a seat large enough for two riders. The motorcycle must have footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear as the rider.

questions.question: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of:
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Travel on the shoulder away from other traffic.

questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes when needed, reduce your speed, and avoid sudden moves. Watch for oily spots, shade, dirt, gravel, and bridges—these have less grip than regular pavement.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not protect as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield cannot replace a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Why are signals important on a motorcycle?

options.text: They are more important than signals on cars and trucks.
They should only be used when another vehicle is right next to you.
They are less important than signals on cars and trucks.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are more important than signals on cars and trucks.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riders are more at risk than car and truck drivers. That is why signals are even more important for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: What do goggles protect?

options.text: Your face just as well as a face shield.
Your face just as well as a windshield.

questions.explanation: Goggles protect only your eyes. A face shield protects your whole face and is better protection. A windshield does not protect your face like goggles or a face shield do.

questions.question: When braking on a motorcycle, which brakes should you use?

options.text: Both brakes at the same time.
Either brake, but never both together.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together to stop your motorcycle. Using both brakes at the same time gives you the best stopping power.

questions.question: What is the best way to survive a motorcycle accident?
questions.explanation: Wearing a helmet is the single most important thing you can do to reduce your risk of injury or death in an accident.

questions.question: What is a danger of braking too hard on a motorcycle?

options.text: Your wheels can lose grip on the road.
You will stop sooner than expected.
It will take you longer to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your wheels can lose grip on the road.
questions.explanation: If you brake too hard, one or both wheels can lose grip on the road, and you may crash.

questions.question: Which of these does not need to be checked before each ride?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, brakes, lights, horn, oil, fluids, and stands. You do not need to check the paint before riding.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?

options.text: Stops your wheels from locking and skidding.
Prevents brakes from working on dry roads.
Warns you when brake pads need to be replaced.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stops your wheels from locking and skidding.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents your wheels from locking and skidding during emergency stops. Sensors detect when a wheel is about to lock. The system releases brake pressure and then reapplies it to give you the best braking power.

questions.question: Which fabric gives motorcycle riders the most protection?
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the best protection when riding a motorcycle.

questions.question: How can you be seen better at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.explanation: Using your headlight and riding in a good lane position helps others see your motorcycle at intersections. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can take action if needed.

questions.question: Which of these is not a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal plates can be slippery. Dry concrete provides good traction for motorcycle tires.
